model: Codex editorial revision with consulted adjective-specific lexical evidence

passages.text: Therefore I, my lord James, after he had said these things and I had made my promise, did not hesitate, as I had been commanded, to present in outline the greater part of the discourses from city to city, which had already been written to you beforehand and sent by him in books, as a kind of reminder, and in this form to send them to you, giving the work the title “Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings among the People.” But I will begin to set it out as I was commanded.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle records Clement’s promise before describing his prompt fulfillment of it.
The expression denotes the bulk or most of the material rather than necessarily all of it.
The phrase concerns reducing or presenting the material by principal points, not merely placing otherwise unabridged material beneath headings.
Literally involving a sign or marker, the phrase describes the summary as an aid to recognition or recollection.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings among the People
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective ἐπιδήμιος itself has the LSJ sense “among the people,” with community, local and resident associations. This broader wording avoids deriving a specific sojourning meaning merely from cognate nouns or verbs. The preceding city-by-city account supplies context, not a lexical equation with travel.
The verb marks the transition from the prefatory letter to presenting the promised material.

source_issues.issue: The accusative participle is syntactically marked with the first-person subject of οὐκ ὤκνησα. It may agree with an understood accusative subject of the dependent infinitives. The nominative ἐπιγράψας would be a conjectural normalization, not an established correction to the supplied reading.

source_issues.source_quote: Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή
source_issues.issue: The title renders ἐπιδημίων with the broad adjective sense “among the people,” attested in LSJ under ἐπιδήμιος (including Iliad 24.262 and the resident-merchants usage in Herodotus 2.39). Local or public preaching is a possible contextual emphasis. An association with Peter’s visits is suggested by the preceding city-by-city description, but a specific sojourning sense is not asserted from cognate words alone. These alternatives remain interpretive, not proposed changes to the Greek.

editorial_revision.actor: Codex assistant, not human scholarly review
editorial_revision.after: Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Preachings among the People.
editorial_revision.scope: Revise the title’s adjective using an actually consulted LSJ entry; retain the separate infinitive/participle note and require fresh independent review.
